units.source: The mobile layout is different than the one on the desktop. Use __TRILIUM_PH_0__ and __TRILIUM_PH_1__ to differentiate between them.

units.source: Detecting horizontal vs. vertical layout__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Reference > Detecting horizontal vs. vertical layout

units.source: The user can select between vertical layout (the classical one, where the launcher bar is on the left) and a horizontal layout (where the launcher bar is on the top and tabs are full-width).
units.context: Reference > Detecting horizontal vs. vertical layout

units.source: Different styles can be applied by using classes at __TRILIUM_PH_0__ level:
units.context: Reference > Detecting horizontal vs. vertical layout

units.source: The two different layouts use different containers (but they are present in the DOM regardless of the user's choice), for example __TRILIUM_PH_0__ and __TRILIUM_PH_1__ can be used to customize the background of the content section.
units.context: Reference > Detecting horizontal vs. vertical layout

units.source: Background/transparency effects on Windows (Mica)__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Reference > Detecting platform (Windows, macOS) or Electron > Background/transparency effects on Windows (Mica)

units.source: Windows 11 offers a special background/transparency effect called Mica, which can be enabled by themes by setting the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ variable at __TRILIUM_PH_1__ level:
units.context: Reference > Detecting platform (Windows, macOS) or Electron > Background/transparency effects on Windows (Mica)

units.source: The value can be either __TRILIUM_PH_0__ (especially useful for the horizontal layout) or __TRILIUM_PH_1__ (ideal for the vertical layout).
units.context: Reference > Detecting platform (Windows, macOS) or Electron > Background/transparency effects on Windows (Mica)

units.source: Do note that the Mica effect is applied at __TRILIUM_PH_0__ level and the theme needs to make the entire hierarchy (semi-)transparent in order for it to be visible. Use the TrilumNext theme as an inspiration.
units.context: Reference > Detecting platform (Windows, macOS) or Electron > Background/transparency effects on Windows (Mica)

units.source: Custom fonts__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Reference > Custom fonts

units.source: The recommended way of using customized fonts is to import a font directly in Trilium. See __TRILIUM_PH_0__Personalizing the font__TRILIUM_PH_1__ for information on how to do so.
units.context: Reference > Custom fonts

units.source: Alternatively, for a theme providing its own font, __TRILIUM_PH_0__Custom resource providers__TRILIUM_PH_1__ can be used: Import a font into Trilium and assign it __TRILIUM_PH_2__ and then import the font in CSS via __TRILIUM_PH_3__. Use __TRILIUM_PH_4__ if you run your Trilium server on a different path than __TRILIUM_PH_5__.

units.source: Adaptive text and table colors__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Reference > Adaptive text and table colors

units.source: Colors applied in a text note, from the font color and background color buttons (see __TRILIUM_PH_0__General formatting__TRILIUM_PH_1__) or from the table and cell properties (see __TRILIUM_PH_2__Tables__TRILIUM_PH_3__), are shown in a shade that suits the theme: the hue stays, while the lightness and the saturation are kept within limits. A theme can change these limits, for example if its page background is much darker or lighter than the one of the built-in themes:
units.context: Reference > Adaptive text and table colors

units.source: Each variable is named __TRILIUM_PH_0__:
units.context: Reference > Adaptive text and table colors

units.source: The role is __TRILIUM_PH_0__ (font color), __TRILIUM_PH_1__ (font background color), __TRILIUM_PH_2__ or __TRILIUM_PH_3__ (tables and cells).
units.context: Reference > Adaptive text and table colors

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__ or __TRILIUM_PH_1__ is the kind of theme the limit applies to, as declared by __TRILIUM_PH_2__.
units.context: Reference > Adaptive text and table colors

units.source: The limit is __TRILIUM_PH_0__ or __TRILIUM_PH_1__ (the CIELAB lightness, from 0 for black to 100 for white), or __TRILIUM_PH_2__ (how saturated the color can be; __TRILIUM_PH_3__ sets no practical limit). Each value must be a plain number, otherwise the colors lose their adaptation.
units.context: Reference > Adaptive text and table colors
